pr_body:
Implements a solution to #57427 to help advance in the GDExtension version of Mono and help make GDExtension easier to use.

* If a Resource type is missing upon load, it will be remembered together with its data (Unless manually overriden). This is implemented by (depending on the case) converting it to a MissingResource type.
* In cases where setting the property will not work because it requires a specific resource type, this is saved as a special metadata.
* If a Node type is missing upon load, it will be also be remembered together with its data (unless deleted). This is done by creating a MissingNode type.
* On save, both the binary and text formats as well as PackedScene recognize MissingNode and MissingResource and convert them to the proper types (so on save they are stored as the correct type).

This feature makes working with GDExtension much easier, as it ensures that missing types no longer cause data loss.

Screens:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6265307/165844362-28136e95-9c1a-4bef-9dd1-f05ba0ad28d9.png)

*Bugsquad edit:*
- Fixes #57427
pr_comments: Is this also useful for editor plugins that are disabled, or `class_name` scripts that are removed?
@Calinou No I don't think so, this is for ClassDB types only. For scripts I think we already have such system, but may not be particularly working in the case you describe.

This is about #57427.

@reduz Please, don't @ me in the commit message. Otherwise, I get spammed notifications 😅
I guess this will also help with alpha changes going forward, like the noise resource issue I had with alpha 5?
@neikeq very sorry, just wanted to reference why this was added. Thanks for the link to the opened issue, replaced it in the description.

Additionally, `get_save_class()` is not overridden in `MissingResource`, so when the Resource saver instance calls it to save the type of the external resource ([binary loc](https://github.com/reduz/godot/blob/0a57f964a357976e023b638e872397ba94123776/core/io/resource_format_binary.cpp#L2021) and [text loc](https://github.com/reduz/godot/blob/0a57f964a357976e023b638e872397ba94123776/scene/resources/resource_format_text.cpp#L1798C57-L1798C57)), it will save the type as "MissingResource" instead of the actual type.

issue_context.title: GDExtension: Scene/resource data can be lost when missing types
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

4.0.alpha1 (31a7ddbf8)

### System information

Ubuntu 21.10, Windows 10, macOS Monterey

### Issue description

Opening and saving a scene or resource that makes use of a GDExtension type will result in any data that depends on that type to be lost, including the type attribute itself. 
This is the same that happens if a built-in type cannot be found.
It's the opposite of **scripts** which rely on placeholder instances to persist data.

There are at least 3 reasons why a GDExtension type may be missing:

- The user may have forgotten to install the extension.
- A bug. Not that I know any in particular, but an unexpected failure to load an extension should not result in the potential of losing scene/resource data.
- **The extension may not be built yet.** This is the most likely scenario, specially when using GDExtension as a replacement for scripting.

For this report, I'm using `godot-cpp` as an example. But my main motivation is C#, as we plan to move it to the GDExtension system.

This bug (or unsupported use case) makes GDExtension unsuitable for scripting.


### Steps to reproduce

Using the [godot-cpp demo example](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-cpp/tree/a2633446536cb3ec9e9b3cb67bc67fa478557752/test):

1. Build the extension.
2. Open the main scene in the Godot editor.
3. Edit the node of type `Example` by modifying the `Custom Position` property value.
4. Save the scene. This should result in a change like the following:
    ```diff
    diff --git a/test/demo/main.tscn b/test/demo/main.tscn
    index 4b6a1a4..02176fc 100644
    --- a/test/demo/main.tscn
    +++ b/test/demo/main.tscn
    @@ -6,6 +6,10 @@
     script = ExtResource( "1_c326s" )
     
     [node name="Example" type="Example" parent="."]
    +group_subgroup_custom_position = Vector2(10, 10)
     
     [node name="Label" type="Label" parent="Example"]
     offset_left = 194.0
    ```
5. Close the editor.
6. Delete the extension (either the `res://example.gdextension` file or the native library).
7. Open the main scene again in the Godot editor.
8. Save the scene. Now, this should result in a change like the following (even if you didn't modify anything yourself):
    ```diff
    diff --git a/test/demo/main.tscn b/test/demo/main.tscn
    index 4b6a1a4..33f8ab0 100644
    --- a/test/demo/main.tscn
    +++ b/test/demo/main.tscn
    @@ -5,7 +5,10 @@
     [node name="Node" type="Node"]
     script = ExtResource( "1_c326s" )
     
    -[node name="Example" type="Example" parent="."]
    +[node name="Example" type="Node" parent="."]
    -group_subgroup_custom_position = Vector2(10, 10)
     
     [node name="Label" type="Label" parent="Example"]
     offset_left = 194.0
    @@ -23,5 +26,3 @@ text = "Click me!"
     __meta__ = {
     "_edit_use_anchors_": false
     }
    -
    -[connection signal="custom_signal" from="Example" to="." method="_on_Example_custom_signal"]
    ```

As you can see, we lost the type of the node (changed from `Example` to `Node`), the modified value of the `group_subgroup_custom_position` property, and a connection to a signal from that node.

This data is not recoverable. Even if you build the extension and open the scene again, it's too late.


### Minimal reproduction project

[godot-cpp demo example](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-cpp/tree/a2633446536cb3ec9e9b3cb67bc67fa478557752/test)

review_comments: `p.pi` hasn't been set yet, so `p.pi.type` will always be NIL here; this should be checking `F.type`
Since this returns in the middle of the loop, all the stuff below the loop gets skipped and missing_resource_properties won't be set
same as above, should be `missing_resource == nullptr`

Nodes report their theme override properties as having `PROPERTY_USAGE_STORAGE` based on whether or not they're actually set. If a theme override property was set to a missing resource, it will be reported as not having `PROPERTY_USAGE_STORAGE` and it will be skipped. This should check if `missing_resource_properties` has the property.
This will never be reached since the above loop returns once we've reached EOF
This should be down in the inner loop and should be assigned to the missing resource properties of `E`; this can currently inadvertently overwrite subresource properties
same as above, should be `missing_resource == nullptr`

If the intent is to check if the parent is NOT missing resource, this should be `missing_resource == nullptr`. 
Currently, if the parent is not a missing resource, this block will be skipped, the property will be set to the missing resource and will probably fail
